name: VSB - Technical University of Ostrava
summary: Ostrava technical university with 175+ years behind it; 16 English-taught bachelor's across geology, materials, economics, IT, engineering and safety.

ib.text: VSB accepts a certified copy of the IB Diploma with no CZK 800 assessment fee. It asks for no IB points or subjects; each faculty ranks on its own test, or on a school average plus an English test.

programmes.name: Applied Geology
programmes.about: Technically oriented geology covering engineering geology, hydrogeology, geophysics and drilling exploration, training operational geologists for field and laboratory work.
programmes.overview: The degree trains operational geologists for all areas of geological research and exploration. You study general geology together with engineering geology and hydrogeology, technical petrography, environmental geochemistry, deposit geology, shallow drilling, applied geophysics and geoinformatics, plus the visualisation and statistical analysis of geological data. Fieldwork is combined with theory, and you learn to plan, organise and evaluate geological work and build geodatabases. Graduates work as field geologists, research technicians, environmental specialists and state administrators, mostly in the private sector, and can continue to master's study.
programmes.ib: Ranked on your penultimate-year school average (Czech-style marks) and an online English test, 21 of 50 to pass (B1); a B1 certificate is needed unless you studied in English.
programmes.selectionNote: Points = 25 x (5 minus your average) plus the English test; best totals fill the places. 2026/27 rules; 2027/28 not yet published. Ask FMG how IB grades convert.

programmes.name: Geoinformatics
programmes.about: GIS and spatial data: digital cartography, remote sensing, satellite positioning, drones and programming in GIS, with geodesy, databases, field work and a bachelor thesis.
programmes.overview: The degree gives knowledge and skills in geoinformatics, geoinformation technologies and geography, and it is taught fully in English with follow-up master's and doctoral studies in the same field. Graduates find work in companies large and small or in public administration, for example as web mapping application developers, data analysts, database specialists or specialists in collecting and distributing geodata.
programmes.ib: Ranked on your penultimate-year school average (Czech-style marks) and an online English test, 21 of 50 to pass (B1); a B1 certificate is needed unless you studied in English.
programmes.selectionNote: Points = 25 x (5 minus your average) plus the English test; best totals fill the places. 2026/27 rules; 2027/28 not yet published. Ask FMG how IB grades convert.

programmes.name: Mineral Economics
programmes.about: Trade, management and economics of raw materials: how deposits are valued, exploited and processed, using modern software and virtual reality, for industry, finance and public-sector roles.
programmes.overview: The degree prepares commodity managers and experts for the mineral raw materials sector, combining technical knowledge of mining with business and management. You study classification of mineral resources, state raw materials policy, extraction and treatment technologies, mining enterprise management, commodity market forecasting, and management systems. Teaching uses modern software, augmented and virtual reality and new laboratories, with study at partner universities abroad possible. Graduates work as managers, business economists, state administration officers and investment advisors in mining and industrial firms, finance and public administration.
programmes.ib: Ranked on your penultimate-year school average (Czech-style marks) and an online English test, 21 of 50 to pass (B1); a B1 certificate is needed unless you studied in English.
programmes.selectionNote: Points = 25 x (5 minus your average) plus the English test; best totals fill the places. 2026/27 rules; 2027/28 not yet published. Ask FMG how IB grades convert.

programmes.name: Mining of Mineral Resources
programmes.about: Open-cast and underground mining, mineral processing and land reclamation, for work in the raw-materials and construction industries, occupational safety or public bodies.
programmes.overview: The degree responds to a mining industry in transition, as coal declines and construction materials and other raw materials gain weight. You study geological exploration and deposit design, surface and underground mining, mineral processing, land reclamation and post-mining restoration, mining law and occupational safety, and the use of mining and transport equipment. Theory is paired with practical problem-solving in the field, and you can steer your focus through electives. Graduates meet the Czech requirements for management posts and work in mining, quarrying, design, safety, public administration and remediation.
programmes.ib: Ranked on your penultimate-year school average (Czech-style marks) and an online English test, 21 of 50 to pass (B1); a B1 certificate is needed unless you studied in English.
programmes.selectionNote: Points = 25 x (5 minus your average) plus the English test; best totals fill the places. 2026/27 rules; 2027/28 not yet published. Ask FMG how IB grades convert.

programmes.name: Waste Management and Mineral Processing
programmes.about: Processing of mineral resources and of waste and secondary raw materials with a circular-economy focus, plus information science and visualisation for process technologies.
programmes.overview: The programme concentrates on processing mineral resources and on current European approaches to waste, with a circular economy and zero-waste outlook. You study mineralogy, chemistry, physics and instrumental analysis, and mechanical, chemical, physical-chemical, biotechnological and thermal processing technologies, plus information science and process visualisation. Teaching combines laboratory work for characterising raw materials and waste with practice in industry. Graduates work as waste managers, technologists, environmental specialists and researchers in industry, state administration, research institutions and municipal services.
programmes.ib: Ranked on your penultimate-year school average (Czech-style marks) and an online English test, 21 of 50 to pass (B1); a B1 certificate is needed unless you studied in English.
programmes.selectionNote: Points = 25 x (5 minus your average) plus the English test; best totals fill the places. 2026/27 rules; 2027/28 not yet published. Ask FMG how IB grades convert.

programmes.name: Materials Engineering
programmes.about: Metals, polymers, structural ceramics and composites: how they are made and processed, and how their structure and properties are tested, with industry projects and internships abroad.
programmes.overview: You study all the main groups of technical materials, metals, polymers, structural ceramics and composites, including their production and recycling, mechanical, physical and chemical properties, microstructure analysis, heat treatment and degradation. Learning is practical, in laboratories comparable to those of developed countries, with chances to work on industrial problems and complete internships abroad. Graduates can continue to the follow-up master's, including a double-degree option with Yokohama National University in Japan, or work in the metallurgical, automotive and engineering industries, in research and development, or in materials testing.
programmes.ib: An oral subject exam (70 points) plus your secondary-school results (30); 51 of 100 needed. B2 English certificate unless all your secondary education was in English.
programmes.selectionNote: Oral exam on published materials topics, in Ostrava or online, 15-19 February 2027; ranked on points up to 20 places.

programmes.name: Nanotechnology
programmes.about: An interdisciplinary bachelor's in the physics and chemistry of nanomaterials: their structure, properties and preparation, for laboratory and industrial work with modern materials.
programmes.overview: The interdisciplinary programme combines theoretical physics and chemistry with a practical focus on the structure and properties of nanomaterials and how they are prepared. Laboratory work teaches the instrumental techniques needed to measure chemical and physical properties, and you learn to interpret experimental results. Graduates can work as qualified assistants in nanomaterials preparation or as operators of specialised instruments in laboratories and materials enterprises, or continue to the master's in Nanotechnology or a related materials programme.
programmes.ib: An oral subject exam (70 points) plus your secondary-school results (30); 51 of 100 needed. B2 English certificate unless all your secondary education was in English.
programmes.selectionNote: Oral exam on published nanotechnology topics, in Ostrava or online, 15-19 February 2027; ranked on points up to 15 places.

programmes.name: Business Administration
programmes.about: How a business is founded, run and grown: management methods, marketing, financial management, sustainability, project work and innovation, with statistics and business data.
programmes.overview: You learn how a business is set up, run and grown, using mathematics, statistics, economics and law as a base, then organisational strategy, management methods, managerial and soft skills, human resources, financial management and accounting, marketing, and legal and tax rules. Innovation, technology and data interpretation come in as well. The programme is broad rather than split into tracks, so it fits many types of company. Graduates take lower and middle-management posts as economic analysts, department heads or financial managers in manufacturing and services, or start their own business.
programmes.ib: Scio GAP test plus the faculty's online English test (B2, 37 of 50); no IB points or subjects asked.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on your best GAP result of four accepted dates (two in autumn 2026, two in early 2027) and the English test score; the English test runs 15-19 February 2027.

programmes.name: Finance
programmes.about: Banking and insurance, financial analysis, tax systems, financial management and investment decisions, leading on to a master's in Finance or other economics programmes.
programmes.overview: Taught in English, the degree covers financial management, cost management and pricing, accounting and taxation, financial markets across banking, investment and insurance, and managerial accounting, balancing theory with practice for middle-level management work. It ends with a state exam and thesis defence. Graduates work as financial managers, investment brokers, tax advisors, bank specialists, accountants or controllers in companies, government and financial institutions, and can continue to the master's in Finance.
programmes.ib: Scio GAP test plus the faculty's online English test (B2, 37 of 50); no IB points or subjects asked.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on your best GAP result of four accepted dates (two in autumn 2026, two in early 2027) and the English test score; the English test runs 15-19 February 2027.

programmes.name: Financial and Accounting Advisory
programmes.about: A professional bachelor's in financial analysis, portfolio management, accounting advice and taxation, for roles in consulting, financial reporting, corporate finance and investment banking.
programmes.overview: This professionally oriented degree follows standards of the CFA and ACCA bodies and teaches by application. You study financial analysis and reporting, corporate finance, portfolio and investment management including derivatives, financial and managerial accounting, direct and indirect taxation, quantitative methods and professional ethics. Practical teaching and professional experience are woven in. Graduates aim at roles such as financial analyst, investment advisor, portfolio manager, controller, auditor and tax advisor in consulting firms, investment funds, banks and corporate finance, and the degree builds toward CFA and ACCA qualifications.
programmes.ib: Scio GAP test plus the faculty's online English test (B2, 37 of 50); no IB points or subjects asked.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on your best GAP result of four accepted dates (two in autumn 2026, two in early 2027) and the English test score; the English test runs 15-19 February 2027.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.about: Software design and development, computer graphics, databases and systems, and intelligent systems, balancing knowledge and skills, with the option of continuing to a master's in Computer Science.
programmes.overview: You study mathematics and theoretical computer science, and three areas of the field: theory, computer systems and applications. Seminars use activating methods and cover technical, social and ethical contexts. Focus areas include software design and development, computer systems and databases, computer graphics, intelligent systems and data analysis, using languages such as C, C++, Java, Python and JavaScript, frameworks, databases, and tools like Git, CUDA and OpenGL. Graduates work as software developers, system administrators, IT analysts and support specialists, or continue to a master's in computer science.
programmes.ib: Scio's NCE maths test at the 50th percentile or better plus an online English test (B2, 38 of 50); no IB points or subjects asked.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked only on the NCE maths percentile; English is pass or fail. Maths test on 30 January or 20 February 2027; English test 15-19 February.

programmes.name: Electrical Engineering
programmes.about: Mathematics, physics, theoretical electrical engineering, electronics, measurement and control, communications and power engineering, preparing operational specialists and a follow-on master's.
programmes.overview: The degree trains operational specialists for all areas of electrical engineering, starting with mathematics, physics and theoretical electrical engineering and moving to electronics, measuring systems, control technology and power engineering. Subjects include digital and microprocessor technology, power semiconductor systems, communication networks, programmable logic controllers, embedded systems and industrial robotics, electrical machines, and the production, transmission and distribution of electricity. Graduates work as designers of electronic equipment, measurement and communication technicians and electrical systems designers, or go on to a specialised master's.
programmes.ib: Scio's NCE maths test at the 50th percentile or better plus an online English test (B2, 38 of 50); no IB points or subjects asked.
programmes.selectionNote: Ranked only on the NCE maths percentile; English is pass or fail. Maths test on 30 January or 20 February 2027; English test 15-19 February.

programmes.name: Safety and Security
programmes.about: Health, safety and environment, industrial safety, fire protection, crisis management and security management, preparing experts in technical and organisational protection against risks.
programmes.overview: The degree covers health, safety and environment, industrial safety, fire protection, crisis management and security, together with management skills. You learn occupational safety, fire protection, security policy and process safety, and how to identify risks, design incident prevention and reduce risk with evidence-based methods. It leads into the HSE Professional master's. Graduates work as industrial and corporate security specialists, emergency management officers and crisis managers in companies of all sizes, government bodies and private organisations.
programmes.ib: GAP test at the 40th percentile or better plus your penultimate-year school average; B2 English certificate unless your schooling was in English.
programmes.selectionNote: Score = 0.7 x GAP percentile + 7.5 x (5 minus your school average); best scores fill 30 places. GAP by 20 February 2027. Ask FSE how IB grades convert.
programmes.closesNote: A second round may run 1-31 March 2027

notes: English-taught bachelor's study costs CZK 50,000 a semester (about EUR 4,000 a year) for EU citizens too; the fee page names no separate EU rate.
VSB's admission-steps page and FAQ still say nostrification is needed; its recognition page takes a certified copy of the IB Diploma with no assessment fee, so quote that page.

Each faculty runs its own entrance test or ranking, so applying to two faculties means two procedures; Civil Engineering and Mechanical Engineering have not published 2027/28 English bachelor's rules.
